name: Ico market

subjectOf.text: The ICO share of total blockchain startup fundraising collapsed from about 80% to roughly 35% by August 2018, recovered only marginally to 40% to 50% through February 2019, and then fell to 20% in March 2019.
subjectOf.abstract: The percentage of ICOs in relation to total fundraising of blockchain startups dropped from 80% to around 35% in August 2018 and only marginally recovered between September 2018 and February 2019 at around 40% to 50% before dropping to 20% in March 2019.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - A Primer on the New Economy (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3406323
scope_conditions: blockchain startup fundraising, March 2018 through March 2019

subjectOf.text: ICOs changed the venture funding market because they provide investors liquidity far faster than the traditional venture capital path to a late IPO or acquisition, letting venture funds capitalize on profits early.
subjectOf.abstract: By contrast, ICOs provide liquidity to investors much faster and allow venture capital funds to capitalize on existing profits early.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - A Primer on the New Economy (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3406323
scope_conditions: venture capital funds invested in crypto start-ups

subjectOf.text: During the ICO boom years the venture capital market in the decentralized technology sector ground to a halt, and the later demise of the ICO market reversed the trend back toward venture funding.
subjectOf.abstract: During the ICO boom years, the venture capital market in the decentralized technology sector ground to a halt.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - A Primer on the New Economy (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3406323
scope_conditions: decentralized technology sector during the ICO boom, roughly March 2017 to June 2018
